scenes.say: A small local model just drove a browser and wrote a web page on a laptop. Should it get the next step too?

scenes.headline: How ARC decides when a small model is enough
scenes.sub: A router that predicts success and tokens, then lets your prices choose
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Peregrin! A viral clip showed a tiny model doing real agent work. Here is the router built to decide when that is good enough.

scenes.title: The model in the clip
scenes.sub: It is LFM3, running inside the Pi harness
scenes.say: Chapter one. The model in the clip.

steps.term: Harness: the loop that runs the tools
steps.say: The launcher names the model: LFM3, one point seven billion parameters, in eight bits, with Pi open beside it. This is not ARC. ARC cannot write a single word.
Pi runs the tools. The model only emits a call to write, with the whole HTML file as its argument, and Pi turns that string into a file.
It checks its own work with a second tool call, then reports. A real loop, from a model this small.
But it never opened the file it was asked to open, and one line of its CSS is silently broken. The user had to ask again.

scenes.title: Why small errors add up
scenes.sub: One slip per step is cheap; twenty steps are not
scenes.say: Chapter two. Why small errors add up.

scenes.title: A run is a product of steps

parts.note: the chance one step goes right
parts.say: Call q the chance that one step goes right.
A run of n dependent steps finishes only if every one of them does, so the chances multiply.

scenes.title: Twenty steps, three step-level skills
scenes.note: chance a 20-step run finishes, q to the 20th
scenes.say: At ninety-five percent a step, a twenty-step task finishes about thirty-six percent of the time. At ninety-nine percent, about eighty-two. The gap between models lives here.

scenes.title: A router in front
scenes.sub: ARC reads the conversation and predicts, before each step
scenes.say: Chapter three. A router in front.

scenes.title: Half a small model, plus small heads

steps.term: Router: picks which model answers next
steps.say: ARC reads the agent's conversation through the first twelve layers of a small Qwen model, left exactly as they were.
Small heads read that state and predict, for every candidate model, its chance of success and how many tokens it will use, in four kinds.
Only when a developer asks a multiple-choice question does the input run on through the upper twelve layers, which were fine-tuned.

legend: One agent run, eight steps, one small local model
Before each step: the predicted chance the local model succeeds
Over the line stays local; under it goes to a cloud model
Prices are applied only where a choice is made
params.tally: two of eight steps go to the cloud

steps.say: Picture the clip's job as a row of steps, all handed to the small model on the laptop.

steps.term: Prefer-local: use local when predicted success clears a threshold
steps.say: Before each step, ARC predicts how likely the local model is to get it right. Reading the stats page and planning the report score lowest.
With the prefer-local rule, every step over the zero point eight five line stays local. The two under it go to a cloud model.
So the cloud bill only lands on the steps that need it, and those are the steps where a small model's slips would compound.

scenes.title: Your prices, not ARC's
scenes.text: pick max of  V x p - C

parts.say: p is ARC's predicted chance that a model succeeds.

parts.note: predicted tokens times your own rates
parts.say: C is its predicted tokens, priced at your own rates. ARC never learns a price.

parts.note: dollars a success is worth to you
parts.say: V is what a success is worth to you. The Sage preset sets four dollars fifty; the Swift preset sets ten cents, and the cheapest model nearly always wins.

scenes.say: Away from the laptop, the utility rule chooses.

scenes.title: Does it hold up?
scenes.sub: The card's headline, recomputed from its own tables
scenes.say: Chapter four. Does it hold up?

steps.say: Here is the hybrid setup against Opus five point five on six benchmarks. Quality holds on code and science.
The bottom row is the share of tasks sent to the local model. But that local model is DeepSeek Flash, spread over several DGX Spark boxes. Not a laptop.

scenes.label: of Opus quality, by the card's own method on its own table
scenes.say: Averaging the card's own per-benchmark ratios gives ninety-eight point five percent, not the headline's ninety-seven point five. Close, but not reproducible as stated.

scenes.title: Where it falls short

items.text: No laptop model among named candidates
items.say: None of the eleven models it names runs on a laptop, and LFM3 is not one of them.
On the one customer-service benchmark, success drops from forty-two point eight to thirty-five point three.
And its question head changes its answer when the options are reordered nineteen percent of the time, twice Jev's rate.

scenes.say: Three places the claim does not reach.

scenes.text: Small agents need a judge per step. ARC is the right shape, but it routes between cloud models today.
scenes.say: A small agent model is useful when something judges it step by step. ARC is the right shape for that judge. Today it routes between cloud models.

recap: The clip is LFM3 in Pi, not ARC

Headline recomputes to 98.5%, with a datacenter local
scenes.say: The clip is LFM3, not ARC. ARC predicts success and tokens, and you set the prices. And its local model lives in a data centre, for now.
